subtopic: A conflict between two team members
subtype: Approach: emotion-aware timing of the discussion [Thinking]
passage: Note from Uday, engineering director. On Monday Manjula stopped by my desk. Two of her people, Tanmay and Divya, had been snapping at each other all week. Manjula wanted to sort it out, but said, "They're both running on empty until Thursday's launch. If I bring it up now, it lands as one more problem." So she waited. The launch went out on Thursday evening. On Friday afternoon Manjula took the two of them to a quiet corner with coffee. I walked past twice: voices low, and at one point a laugh. By Monday Manjula told me they had agreed who reviews what. All I did was leave them alone and approve a half-day for the team.

qa.q: When did Manjula meet Tanmay and Divya to talk?
qa.a: Manjula took them to a quiet corner on Friday afternoon.

qa.q: Why did Manjula wait before raising the problem, and what was she worried about?
qa.a: Manjula worried that Tanmay and Divya were too exhausted before launch, and that raising it then would feel like one more problem.

qa.q: What else could Manjula do to keep the peace, and why?
qa.a: Manjula could check in with each of them a week later, because a calm talk may still need a follow-up to settle into habit.

qa.q: How might Divya have felt about the timing of the talk?
qa.a: Divya probably felt relieved and more open, since the pressure of the launch was over and there was space to speak calmly.

grounding: Illustrates a lead seeing that two colleagues are stressed by a release and waiting until the day after launch to talk, when the discussion is calm.

subtopic: A conflict between two team members
subtype: Approach: emotion-aware timing of the discussion [Thinking]
passage:
Tuesday night

Nikita and Joel nearly bit each other's heads off in standup again. Something about who broke the staging server. I almost called them both into the meeting room right then.
Then I looked at them properly. Nikita hasn't gone home before ten all week. Joel was eating lunch standing up at his keyboard. Launch is Thursday. Anything I say now will land on two exhausted people, and they'll hear blame, not questions.
So I'm waiting. Friday morning, after launch, I'll book a quiet half hour with chai and ask what's going on between them.
Friday update: glad I waited. Both came in slept and a bit lighter. Joel even laughed about the server. We talked it through calmly and agreed who resets staging.
— Aditi

qa.q: Why did Aditi hold back from calling Nikita and Joel into the meeting room on Tuesday?
qa.a: Aditi was worried that two exhausted, stressed people would hear blame rather than questions, and chose patience over a frustrated rush to fix it.

qa.q: What else could Aditi have done if the fighting was hurting the launch itself?
qa.a: Aditi could have set a quick, practical rule for staging resets before launch, keeping the deeper talk for Friday.

qa.q: How might the Friday talk feel to Joel compared with a Tuesday one?
qa.a: Joel is rested and calmer after launch, so he can laugh about the server and discuss it rather than defend himself while under pressure.

grounding: It shows a lead noticing that both colleagues are stressed by a release and waiting until after launch, so the talk happens calmly.

subtopic: A conflict between two team members
subtype: Approach: emotion-aware timing of the discussion [Thinking]
passage:
Sonali: Deepika, can I think out loud for a sec?
Deepika: always
Sonali: Karan and Mehul had a proper shouting match over the test data today
Deepika: yikes. you talking to them tonight?
Sonali: that was my plan. but the client demo is tomorrow at 11 and both of them are running on no sleep 😣
Sonali: if I sit them down now, it'll just be round two
Deepika: so after the demo?
Sonali: day after. give them one normal night first. the argument isn't going anywhere, but their stress will drop
Deepika: makes sense
(two days later)
Sonali: talked to them this morning
Deepika: and??
Sonali: completely different. calm voices, both admitted they'd been snappy. we agreed who owns the test data 🙂
Deepika: timing is everything

qa.q: What time was the client demo?
qa.a: The client demo was at 11 the next day.

qa.q: What was Sonali worried about when talking to Karan and Mehul that night?
qa.a: Sonali was worried that, running on no sleep, they would turn the talk into round two of the fight, and felt it was better to wait until the stress dropped.

qa.q: Which other approach might suit Sonali if the fighting had started to affect the demo?
qa.a: Sonali could separate their tasks for the demo day only, so work continues, and still hold the proper talk once the pressure has eased.

qa.q: What was the delayed talk like for Karan and Mehul?
qa.a: After a normal night and the demo done, they could speak calmly and admit they'd been snappy instead of defending themselves.

grounding: It shows a lead seeing that two colleagues are stressed by a deadline and waiting until the day after before discussing the issue calmly.
